analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md (date bump, drain-acknowledgement wording near head line 443, and a new handshake-deadline table row near head line 1943). The supplied units are BASE text for lines 806-1725 and do not include any changed lines, so no changed code or control was examined directly. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is complete.

Security-relevant doc claims: (1) A drain may complete without a coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and the provider has no registered coordinator session. A registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. This is a lifecycle/availability semantic related to the T-053 and TB-002 areas. It is unclear whether the implementation in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift could skip the acknowledgement for a session that is registered but momentarily disconnected, causing the coordinator to lose terminal usage or billing data. That source was not supplied, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. (2) The 30 s coordinator handshake deadline (CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift) is a DoS-hardening control on TB-002. It needs no threat-model change, but the implementation was not supplied.

The base text in the supplied units (autopilot, doctor, stop/restart, report, logout/unenroll) is pre-existing and unchanged by this PR. I report nothing from it. Nothing in the diff weakens attestation, encryption, or the prefix cache (T-041), and no new attack surface is introduced by documentation alone. The next pass should check that the code matches the documented drain and handshake behavior if the implementation files are part of the same PR.
